Site handover23-Dec-2025

Scope: collector and local roads, potable water, sewage, storm drainage, irrigation, TSE, medium voltage, street lighting and telecom networks, a sewage pump station, storm drainage ponds, the boundary fence and guard room, and utility buildings, in the 2nd Industrial City in Dammam.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. The weekly report (WPR-39) gives 37.09% actual against 68.43% planned in the original baseline and 54.12% in the revised plan. Against last week's report (32.47%) the project gained 4.62% this week.

The forecast delay grew to 113 days. The weekly report and the P6 update both now forecast completion on 15-Jun-2027, a week later than last week, against the contract date of 22-Feb-2027; the completion milestone has −86 days of float in P6. The networks are moving: sewage, storm drainage and potable water pipes were laid for the first time (331 m, 500 m and 390 m). To finish on 22-Feb-2027 the remaining 62.91% must be done in 15 weeks, about 4.19% a week.

Data notes

  • Data date: WPR-39, the P6 update, the procurement tracker and the look-ahead are all dated 03-Nov-2026 (a Tuesday), five days after last week's 29-Oct-2026. The Milestones sheet now shows "Contract Weeks 0 of 0", so the week number is (03-Nov-2026 − 23-Dec-2025) ÷ 7 = 315 days, week 45.
  • Man-hour total: the cover and Progress sheets still drop Sewage's 516 man-days (total 18,474 instead of 18,990 in P6). With the full budget, physical progress is 36.08%, as on the Physical-Chart Data sheet. The headline uses the reported 37.09%. The P6 update itself gives 6,711.7 earned man-days (35.34%) against 6,852 in the weekly report; the 140 man-day gap is all in procurement.
  • This week's gain: the cumulative figure rose by 853 man-days (4.62%), but the cover sheet's weekly column gives 542 earned against 619 planned (2.93% against 3.35%).
  • The original-plan figure is unchanged at 68.43% (12,641.76 man-days) for the second week, so the baseline SPI does not move with time. The chart sheet's baseline is 73.84% at the end of October and 85.41% at the end of November.
  • The Milestones sheet's "latest plan" dates are now earlier than the baseline for most networks (for example medium voltage 11-Jan-2027 against 07-Mar-2027), and its days-change column is measured against them; the table above measures against the baseline.
  • The Conclusion sheet labels cost-based progress as "actual"; it is not used in this report. Its storm network total changed from 5,560 m to 4,635 m and its potable water total from 2,439 m to 2,359 m, and its roads earthworks (637,536 m³) is unchanged from last week against 802,396 m³ on the Major Quantities sheet.
  • Quantities: on the Major Quantities sheet the network pipes, manholes, blockwork, bituminous coating and joint sealant are pro-rated (each line in a group carries the same percentage, for example 85.6% for blockwork, coating and sealant), so they are not measured values. Network lengths are taken from the Conclusion sheet instead.
  • Procurement tracker: sewage manhole covers fell from 42 of 42 last week to 0 of 42; the fire hydrant total changed from 45 to 18; several expected delivery dates are in December 2027 or in the past (telecom ducts 30-Jan-2026); the fence concrete figure (8,300 m³) and its 30% note are unchanged. The quantity-details sheet was not included this week.
  • Safety: "this month" man-hours (9,000) are lower than this week's (18,000). The HSE inspection sheet still carries project ID DAMT-02-001.
  • Invoices: the cover sheet shows 2 invoices and 0 paid; the invoice log lists 3 invoices with the first two paid (3,596,613.90 SAR), references DAMT-02-001 and gives a revised contract value of 21,100,000. Unchanged from last week.
  • The "major activities this week" list on the photo summary sheet is the same as last week apart from two lines.
  • The photos have no date or GPS stamp. Two of the four new photos show the same concrete ring from two sides. The PowerPoint file in the upload could not be opened (damaged archive), and a temporary Excel lock file (~$) was uploaded by mistake.
